title: Fifty-Three Years in Syria. In Two Volumes. Volume I
creator: Henry Harris Jessup, D.D.; Introduction by James S. Dennis, D.D.
publisher: New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell Company; London and Edinburgh
content: Volume I of two of a missionary's memoir of Syria, chapters I-XVIII. Editorial matter: Introduction signed James S. Dennis at lines 307-475, with a note on the author's death at lines 479-492; contents of both volumes at lines 670-816. The text runs from line 1000 to line 22091; there is no index in this volume. Divisions: in chapter III, 'The Seven Pioneers of Syria Mission Work' (from line 1864), section II (lines 2044-2256) tells of Pliny Fisk. Chapter IV (lines 3904-4576) tells of the Arabic Bible and its translators. Asaad es Shidiak has no section of his own; he is named at lines 1773, 2069, 2133, 2314 and 2373 and later.
locus: section 'II. Pliny Fisk, the Linguist and Preacher' at lines 2044-2256; chapter IV on the Arabic Bible and its translators at lines 3904-4576; the rest not mapped
flags: The title page prints no year; 1910 is the copyright notice at line 146. The contents list an index at page 821, which belongs to volume II.

title: A History of the Plymouth Brethren
creator: William Blair Neatby, M.A.
content: A history of the Plymouth Brethren in sixteen chapters, by a writer who is not Darby. Editorial matter: the author's Preface at lines 88-233, which says the work is partly based on his articles 'Darby and Darbyism' in the British Weekly; contents from line 241. The text runs from line 296 to line 14204; a Bibliographical Appendix follows from line 14207. Mixed voices: Darby and other writers are quoted inside the narrative. John Nelson Darby's birth is told at line 792; chapter V treats 'Darby in Vaud' (from line 3411), chapter IX 'The Supremacy of Darby' (lines 7779-8463), and chapter XII 'Darby's Strange Corrective to Newtonianism' (from line 10076).
locus: chapter IX, 'The Epoch of Exclusivism - The Supremacy of Darby', at lines 7779-8463; the rest not mapped

title: A Retrospect of the First Ten Years of the Protestant Mission to China, (now, in connection with the Malay, denominated, the Ultra-Ganges Missions.) Accompanied with Miscellaneous Remarks on the Literature, History, and Mythology of China, &c
creator: William Milne
publisher: Malacca: Printed at the Anglo-Chinese Press
content: An account of the mission's first ten years by one of its missionaries, who writes of himself as 'Mr. M.' and quotes his own journal. Editorial matter: the author's Preface from line 197, which acknowledges a manuscript by the Rev. R. Morrison; Introduction at line 345. Divisions: numbered sections from Section I (line 604) to Section XVIII (line 14412); an Appendix of numbered pieces at lines 15093-18519, the first an account of the Malay books. No contents list was found. The baptism of 'Leang-kung-fah', a Chinese printer to the mission, on November 3, 1816, with the questions put to him and his weekly reading with the author, is told at lines 8198-8347.
locus: the conversion and baptism of Leang-kung-fah, with the journal extract of Nov. 3, at lines 8198-8347; the rest not mapped
flags: OCR is poor in places: long s is read as f, many words are garbled, and the front matter (lines 13-345) is hard to read; the headings of sections XIV and XV were not found by search. A Harvard library slip closes the file.

title: The Story of Uganda and the Victoria Nyanza Mission. With a map and illustrations
creator: Sarah Geraldina Stock
content: A history of the Church Missionary Society's mission in Uganda in fourteen chapters. Editorial matter: an unsigned Introduction at lines 45-214; contents at line 217, followed by a list of illustrations. The text runs from Chapter I at line 316 to line 7707; a catalog of the publisher's books fills lines 7713-9183. Mixed voices: extracts from the missionaries' letters, among them Mackay and Ashe, are printed inside the narrative. Chapter IX, 'The Great Persecution', begins at line 4287, and in it the death of 'Balikudembe Mukasa, the king's head page', sentenced to be burnt alive two days after November 13, 1885, is told at lines 4386-4413. The file calls the Catholic missionaries 'the Romish priests'.
locus: the death of Balikudembe Mukasa at lines 4386-4413; the rest not mapped

title: Le Cardinal Lavigerie et ses œuvres d'Afrique. Nouvelle édition complètement refondue
creator: L'abbé Félix Klein, professeur à l'Institut catholique de Paris
publisher: Tours: Alfred Mame et fils, éditeurs
content: A life of Cardinal Lavigerie in French, in thirteen chapters; the title page calls it a new edition, completely recast. Editorial matter: a list of the author's other works at lines 43-68; an Avant-propos at lines 104-283, made up of the author's note dated Paris, 6 January 1897, further matter signed Félix Klein, and from line 247 a letter to the author from Mgr Livinhac dated Rodez, 14 July 1893. The text runs from Chapter I at line 294 to 'FIN' at line 14316; the table of contents is at the end, from line 14360. Chapter VII, 'L'Ouganda', begins at line 6707, and in it the arrest and burning of 'Charles Louanga', head of a group of royal pages, is told at lines 7154-7220.
locus: Charles Louanga and the pages arrested, bound and burned at lines 7154-7220; the rest not mapped

title: Das Bulgarische Exarchat und der Mazedonische Kirchenstreit. Inaugural-Dissertation zur Erlangung der Doktorwürde bei der Juristischen Fakultät der Universität Leipzig
creator: Kurt Scheffler, Dragoman der Kaiserl. Botschaft in Konstantinopel
content: A German doctoral dissertation in law on the Bulgarian Exarchate and the church dispute in Macedonia. Editorial matter: contents at lines 65-85, a list of sources and literature from line 88, and a foreword (Vorwort) from line 153. Divisions: three main parts, the second on the Bulgarian Exarchate (from line 761) and the third on the Macedonian church dispute (from line 2205); the text ends at line 2493. The firman of 11 March 1870, articles 1-11 with its closing clause, is printed in German, translated by the author from the Turkish text, at lines 1117-1263. The election of 'Anthimos', archbishop of Widdin, as exarch on 23 February 1872, and the break with the Patriarchate, are told at lines 1319-1347.
locus: the firman of 11 March 1870 in German, articles 1-11, at lines 1117-1263; the election of the exarch Anthimos and the events of 1872 at lines 1319-1347; the rest not mapped
flags: Lines 49-53 are the Internet Archive's own digitization notice (dated 2026), not part of the edition. No author's life (vita) is printed at the end.

title: Raccolta di concordati su materie ecclesiastiche tra la Santa Sede e le autorità civili
creator: not named on the title page
content: A collection of concordats between the Holy See and civil powers, numbered I-CXXXIII in order of date, each in its own language (Latin, Italian, French and Spanish among them) with source notes in Italian. Editorial matter: Avvertenza from line 55, signed 'Il compilatore Sac. Angelo Mercati'; list of the concordats from line 179; texts from line 1139; errata and indexes from line 78102. No. CVIII, the concordat of 28 March 1860 with Haiti, runs from line 61913 to line 62630: preamble and articles 1-18 in Italian and French (to line 62499), notes, then a French letter of Pierre Faubert and Cardinal Antonelli's Italian reply (lines 62520-62623). 'Fabre Geffrard' is named in the preamble (lines 61924, 61938, 61952, 61965) and in the source note at line 62626.
locus: the concordat with Haiti of 28 March 1860, preamble and articles 1-18 in Italian and French, at lines 61913-62499; the letter of Faubert and the reply of Antonelli, 28 March 1860, at lines 62520-62623; the rest not mapped
flags: The title page names no compiler; the Avvertenza is signed by Angelo Mercati (lines 128-130). In the Haiti text the Italian and French columns are interleaved by the OCR, so the articles do not read in one run.

title: A Narrative of Captivity in Abyssinia; with some account of the late Emperor Theodore, his country and people
creator: Henry Blanc, M.D., M.R.C.S.E., F.A.S.L., etc., Staff Assistant-Surgeon Her Majesty's Bombay Army (lately on special duty in Abyssinia)
content: A captive's own account of his imprisonment in Abyssinia, in twenty chapters and a Conclusion. Editorial matter: contents from line 71; the author's Preface, dated London, July 23, 1868, from line 372, which says parts of his report to the Government of Bombay are included. The text runs from line 433 to line 15623; the Conclusion begins at line 15450. Chapter I (lines 433-1279) tells of the Emperor Theodore's rise, rule, character and household. Chapter XV begins at line 10557 with the death of 'Abouna Salama' on the 25th of October and a sketch of his life and his quarrel with Theodore (lines 10569-11132).
locus: chapter I on the Emperor Theodore at lines 433-1279; the death and career of Abouna Salama at lines 10569-11132; the rest not mapped
flags: Lines 32-36 are the Internet Archive's own digitization notice, not part of the edition. A library due-date slip closes the file.

title: The Martyr Church: a narrative of the introduction, progress, and triumph of Christianity in Madagascar, with notices of personal intercourse and travel in that island. Third thousand
creator: Rev. William Ellis, author of 'Polynesian Researches,' 'Three Visits to Madagascar,' &c., &c.
content: A history of Christianity in Madagascar in fourteen chapters, marked 'Third Thousand' on the title page. Editorial matter: the author's Preface at lines 108-167; contents from line 170. The text runs from Chapter I at line 580; chapter XIV ends at line 15178, a Postscript follows at lines 15183-15518, and the publisher's book list begins at line 15523. The first queen is proclaimed at lines 2557-2571 and her character is summed up at lines 8749-8798; between those points the narrative mostly calls her 'the queen'. A second queen takes the name Ranavalona in chapter XIV (lines 13988-15178), which tells of her coronation and baptism. The OCR mostly prints the name as 'Eanavalona'.
locus: Ranavalona proclaimed queen at lines 2557-2571; the first queen's character at lines 8749-8798; chapter XIV on the second Ranavalona at lines 13988-15178; the rest not mapped
flags: The OCR reads capital R as E in many names ('Eanavalona', 'Eadama', 'Easoherina'), so a search for 'Ranavalona' finds few of the places.
